blocks.content: The Vedic Age represents a crucial phase in ancient Indian history during which the foundations of Indian society, religion, culture, and philosophy were laid. This period is named after the Vedas, the oldest religious texts of India. The Vedic Age is generally dated between 1500 BC and 600 BC and is divided into two distinct phases: the Early Vedic Age and the Later Vedic Age.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Vedic period is broadly divided into the Early Vedic Period (1500–1000 BCE) and the Later Vedic Period (1000–500 BCE).
The four major Vedas are Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda, forming the core of Shruti literature.
Early Vedic society was predominantly pastoral and egalitarian, where democratic assemblies like Sabha and Samiti played key political roles.
The usage of Iron (Shyama Ayas) during the Later Vedic Period enabled major agricultural expansion in the Gangetic plains.
Social structure transformed from flexible clan-based varnas in the Early Vedic Period to rigid, birth-based varna divisions in the Later Vedic Period.

blocks.content: The primary sources of information about the Vedic Age are the Vedic texts. These include the four Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, and Upanishads.

cells: Oldest Veda; hymns in praise of gods

blocks.content: The Vedic Age is divided into two phases based on changes in society, economy, and polity.
The Early Vedic Age is also known as the Rigvedic Age. The Aryans lived mainly in the region known as Sapta Sindhu (land of seven rivers). Their society was primarily pastoral in nature.
The Vedic Age marked the fundamental transition from a pastoral nomadic society to settled agrarian kingdoms in ancient India.

The political organization was tribal. The basic unit was the family, followed by grama (village), vis (clan), jana (tribe), and rashtra. The king was known as Raja and was a tribal chief, not an absolute monarch.
Sabha and Samiti were popular assemblies. Sabha dealt with judicial and administrative matters, while Samiti was a general assembly where the king was elected or approved.
The economy was primarily pastoral. Cattle were the main measure of wealth. Agriculture was known but not the primary occupation.
Early Vedic society was largely egalitarian. The Varna system was flexible and based on occupation. Women enjoyed a respectable position and participated in religious activities.

rows: Decline in status; excluded from political assemblies

blocks.content: Religion was simple and nature-based. Major gods included Indra, Agni, Varuna, Soma, and Surya. There were no temples or idol worship.
The Later Vedic Age witnessed significant changes in society, economy, polity, and religion. Agriculture became the main occupation and society became more complex.
Kingship became hereditary and more powerful. Large kingdoms emerged. Popular assemblies declined in importance.
The Varna system became rigid. Society was divided into four Varnas: Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras. The status of women declined.
Agriculture became the main occupation. Iron tools were used. Trade and crafts developed.
Rituals and sacrifices became complex and expensive. Upanishadic philosophy emphasized knowledge (jnana) over rituals.

items: Rigveda is the oldest Veda containing 1028 hymns divided into 10 Mandalas; the 3rd Mandala contains the Gayatri Mantra composed by Viswamitra.
Sabha was an elite assembly of elders, whereas Samiti was a general political assembly of the common people in Rigvedic times.
Iron was referred to as 'Shyama Ayas' or 'Krishna Ayas' in Later Vedic literature, whereas 'Ayas' referred to copper or bronze.
The Battle of Ten Kings (Dasrajan War) was fought on the banks of the river Parushni (Ravi).

blocks.content: Education was imparted through the Gurukul system. Students lived with their teachers and education focused on religion, philosophy, warfare, and moral values.
Women enjoyed a high status in the Early Vedic Age, participating in rituals and education. In the Later Vedic Age, their position declined due to social rigidity.
The Vedic Age laid the foundation of Indian civilization. Its social, religious, and philosophical ideas deeply influenced later Indian history.
Oldest Veda – Rigveda. Pastoral economy – Early Vedic Age. Agrarian economy – Later Vedic Age. Popular assemblies – Sabha and Samiti. Four Varnas – Later Vedic Age.
